title: Piano versus guitar in the rhythm section; Bernard Addison
summary: Foster prefers piano now since few guitarists play chords, praises one guitarist and recalls New Orleans pianist-guitarists.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah, well, that's a good name that you had. I was going to ask more about the rhythm section and working with the rhythm section, would you rather have a piano? Like in the old days they only had guitar and bass and drums maybe, but now they all have a piano.
Well, I'd rather have piano now because we haven't got no good guitar players. We haven't got none of the younger guys now playing your six string chords on guitar.
That's Jimmy. You see, none of that they deal, you get the guitar players, play the full chords.

Well, they just play solos and things like that. Yeah, most of them want to play solos and I can't stand those lectures. You see now, Johnny, Johnny Sincero is the one we got left. Now we got one guy around New York, who was the best around right now, Bernard Anderson.
Yeah, I was going to ask that.

Yeah, I see. He's pretty good. You see, he's the best one. And I made him get a guitar. I used to sit up with him all night when he was on band. See, I used to sit up with him all night, he and I, draft him with his guitars, and I'd take the bass over to his room. We'd like to do that. I didn't put that one now, we'd make so much noise, he'd get the bass. Three or four o'clock in the morning. See? You get six string chords, the other guys are going to play a whole lot of melody. See? Because the guitar is a rhythm. See? And we played everything without a piano. It's like I told guys back in those days. Piano players, you had to learn how to play something if you wanted to play in them bands, the violin and stuff. But most of your violin players, back to the plate piano. See? And most of them you get that player is playing piano.
Like Tommy, what's his name, Tommy?
What's Tommy's name? Thomas- Jefferson? No. Thomas. Yeah, Thomas, in New Orleans. Thomas- Oakland- Oakland- Uptown he played piano and guitar. Tom.
Was it Tom Benton? Oh, Benton.
Buddy Christian used to play piano and guitar.
Yeah, he still. Well, Tom Benton too. Tom Benton, yeah.
